2–60  3937 0457- 104 Balance Sheet Rule Off Dates (GLROM)  
A balance sheet is us ually ruled off after the end of an accounting period when the books are fully 
reconciled. The effect is to prevent any further changes to the balance sheet for the accounting 
period.  
The Balance Sheet Rule Off Dates (GLROM) screen is used to set up the in itial balance sheet rule 
off dates and to update the balance sheet rule off date for an accounting period. Postings can only be back valued up to and including the balance sheet rule off date currently in use.  
For example, if you want to close the April ac counting period, then you set the “Current Rule Off 
Date” field to April 30th. The actual date on which you change the rule off date is at your 
discretion, but it must be after April 30th. As soon as you set the rule off date for the period, no 
more back -valued postings or adjustments will be accepted for that period.  
The original balance sheet rule off dates must be set up using the Balance Sheet Rule Off Dates (GLROM) screen before installation has been completed. To achieve this, switch 'on' the  “Instal lation Complete” field.  
After adding the initial rule off dates and completing other installation tasks, the Installation Complete indicator can be set on the System Parameters (SPMTR)  screen (see the Guide to 
Setting Up ). Users of the Retail syst em should see System Parameters (SPMTR)  in the Guide to 
Setting Up the Retail System . 
Updating of rule off dates can be done at any time provided the initial rule off dates were set up 
before installation was completed.  
The Balance Sheet Rule Off Dates (GLROM) screen has an inquiry section where the previous 
and current rule off dates are displayed, as well as an update section where the rule off dates can be amended.  
If you change the “Previous Rule Off Date”, you must also change the “Current Rule Off Date”.  
If you are only changing the “Current Rule Off Date”, it must be greater than the “Previous Rule Off Date”.  
If both dates are being changed:  
• The “Previous Rule Off Date” must be set to the “Current Rule Off Date” as shown in the 
inqui ry section  
• The “Current Rule Off Date” entered must be greater than the “Previous Rule Off Date” 
entered.

OPERATIONS REFERENCE CARD 
About Urbis  
Use of the product name Urbis is due to be phased out as part of the Unisys re- branding 
exercise. The replacement will be the generic term of “Banking Back -Office Processing” 
solution or “Banking Back -Office” for short. To provide continuity with existing product 
documentation, the name Urbis is used within this document, but is synonymous with 
Banking Back -Office solution.   
HOW TO LOG ON  
On the System Logon Screen, enter your:  
 Usercode 
 Password  
 Station  Password  
 
Click OK or press Return  
 The Previous Log On Screen is displayed. Click OK on this screen.  
HOW TO SELECT A FUNCTIONAL AREA  
When you first log on, click the Front Office icon to view the functional areas available. 
Select the appropriate icon to view the menus of a functional area.  
Note :  If you are using the Front Office you must select the Front Office icon to view the 
 menus available.  
This card shows the screens available within each functional area.  
HOW TO SELE CT A SCREEN 
Screens are listed under dropdown menus. Click on the menu to open it then select a screen name from the list. Alternatively, use the Call Screen (F5)  option listed under the Common 
menu  and enter the four or five letter mnemonic of the screen and click OK. 
HOW TO COMPLETE DATA ENTRY SCREENS  
Adding Data  
1. Select the screen you want.  
2. Complete the data entry fields and click OK. 
Changing Data  
1. Select the screen you want.  
2. Complete the recall fields and click Inquire . 
3. Change the data and  click Change . 
Recalling Data 
1. Select the screen you want.  
2. Complete the recall fields and click OK (click Inquire  if appropriate). The inquiry 
is then displayed.

Deleting Data 
1. Select the screen you want.  
2. Complete the recall fields and click Inquire. Check that this is the data you want to 
delete.  
3. Click Delete.  
4. The system prompts you to confirm the deletion. Click OK to delete the data.  
Correcting Errors  
Error messages are displayed on the bottom line of the screen or in a separate window: the 
Application Error window. When you have finished reading the errors in this window, click OK to close it and return to the original screen.  
To correct errors, you may need to consult your supervisor.  
HOW TO MAKE AN ONLINE INQUIRY  
1. Select the inquiry screen you require.  
2. Complete the mandatory fields and optional fields.  
3. Click OK (click Inquire  if appropriate). The inquiry details are then displayed.  
HOW TO SELECT A CLIENT AND AN ACCOUNT  
When you are performing a banking task, you will often need to select a client or an account 
so that their details can be moved from screen to screen without the need for re- keying the 
data.  
Selecting a Client  
1. Select the client screen you require. For example, the Client Details -  Personal 
(CIPER) screen. The C lient Identification (CACII) screen is then displayed.  
2. Complete identification field(s) according to the information you have available.  
3. Click OK. The Client Selection (CASLI) screen is then displayed showing details 
of any clients that meet your ide ntification criteria.  
4. Use the Select Client field to enter the number displayed next to one of the clients.  
5.  Click OK. The screen that you entered in step 1 will display details of your selected 
client.  
(The client selected will be used for every subsequ ent client screen until you clear 
the client via Clear Memory in the Common Menu).  
Selecting an Account  
1. Select the account screen you require. For example, the Client Account Maintenance (CAHDR) screen. The Account Identification (CAIDI) screen is then displayed.  
2. Complete the identification fields according to the information you have available.  
3. Click OK. The screen that you entered in step 1 will display details of your selected 
account.  
 (The client selected will be used for every subsequent client screen until you clear the client via Clear Memory in the Common Menu).  
HOW TO PRODUCE A REPORT  
1. Select Run Report  from the Common Menu.  
2. Complete the fields on the Report Run Parameters screen and click OK. If the 
report has options, the Run Time Options  screen is displayed.  
3. Enter the options and click OK. The report is then produced.

1. The Core Challenge — Managing Fragmentation
 Core Banking Silos: 12 regional endpoints split across two completely different, legacy backends—Urbis (7 regions
including Bahrain, Milan, London, NY) and Ambit (5 regions including Egypt, Algeria).
 Vendor Dependencies: ABC Cash runs on a third-party SaaS platform managed entirely by external MGS vendors.
 Tooling Gaps: Operational workflows require slow, manual tracking across ServiceNow (ABC Hub), external Vendor
Jira, and PingOne identity/OIDC flows.
 Operational Cost Risk: Feeding raw, uncompressed system logs directly into AI agent workflows scales token
consumption expenses exponentially.

2. The Solution Shift — Web Chat vs. Autonomous CLI
 Standard Web-Based UI Limits: Excellent at isolated, generic tasks but cannot see our infrastructure. Requires human
engineers to manually sanitize and paste sensitive log structures into a browser window.
 Claude Code Command Line Engine: Runs natively inside our secure terminal server environments. It can directly
execute shell commands, parse codebase directories, and edit files safely under strict programmatic boundaries.
 The Implementation Tool: Instead of human teams writing individual validation pipelines manually over several
months, Claude Code acts as our primary autonomous engine to program, audit, and deploy the infrastructure
wrappers.

6. The Budget Guardrail — Vision-Grid Proxy
 The Context Accumulation Problem: Passing long historical Jira conversations, multi-system runbooks, and deep
server log dumps back and forth continuously creates an unsustainable text-token billing model.
 The Vision Loophole: The proxy intercepts text payloads exceeding 6,000 characters and flattens them into
ultra-dense, monospaced pixel grids. Advanced multi-modal LLMs price images on a rigid geometric bounding box
flat-rate rather than data frequency.
 Fiscal Efficiency: Packs up to 3.1 characters per token (compared to roughly 1 character per text token), delivering a
verified 60% to 70% reduction in long-term model token costs.
